source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Start as soon as possible, ideally within 48 hours; later treatment may still help selected high-risk patients","B":"Wait until at least 48 hours have passed because early antiviral treatment provides less clinical benefit","C":"Delay treatment until influenza symptoms are nearly resolved so medication adverse effects are minimized","D":"Use timing only for dosing convenience because treatment benefit is unrelated to symptom duration"}}
source_row.rationale: CDC 2026 guidance states that influenza antiviral treatment provides the greatest benefit when started early, especially within 48 hours. However, treatment can still provide benefit after 48 hours in hospitalized patients, patients with severe or progressive illness, and people at increased risk for complications.
source_row.source_detail: Updated March 10, 2026: benefit greatest when started early, especially within 48 hours; later treatment can still benefit hospitalized/severe/progressive/high-risk patients.
source_row.source_name: CDC — Influenza Antiviral Medications: Summary for Clinicians
source_row.stem: A client with influenza asks about the importance of antiviral timing. Which teaching is most accurate?
